facts.statement: Scalamagnus is known from a single species, S. tropicensis, represented by one skull and two partial skeletons.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species S. tropicensis, known from a skull and two partial skeletons.

facts.statement: The fossils were collected between 2003 and 2005 by the Museum of Northern Arizona from a single locality in the Tropic Shale of Utah.
facts.quote: It was collected between 2003 and 2005 by the Museum of Northern Arizona from a single locality within the Tropic Shale of Utah

facts.statement: The holotype is an almost complete, well-preserved skeleton measuring 3.2 meters in length that includes most of the skull.
facts.quote: The holotype MNA V10046, an almost complete, well-preserved 3.2 m long skeleton including most of the skull

facts.statement: Scalamagnus lived during the early Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 93.5 to 91 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating to the early Turonian stage of the early Late Cretaceous, about 93.5-91 million years ago

facts.statement: A 2023 study reclassified the species D. tropicensis into its own new genus, Scalamagnus.
facts.quote: A 2023 study assigns D. tropicensis to a new genus, Scalamagnus.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton is associated with 289 gastroliths, a feature unusual for most polycotylids which typically lack such stones.
facts.quote: The holotype is associated with 289 gastroliths, which is unusual in comparison to most polycotylid skeletons that generally lack gastroliths.

facts.statement: Most of the gastroliths were small, with about three-quarters weighing less than 2 grams and a mean mass of 1.9 grams.
facts.quote: About three-quarters of the stones weighed less than 2 grams, with the mean mass and median mass of the stones respectively estimated at 1.9 grams and 0.8 grams.

facts.statement: The characteristics of the gastroliths suggest the animal obtained them from rivers along the western side of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: suggesting that this individual was obtaining its stones from rivers located along the western side of the Western Interior Seaway.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Scalamagnus spans from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago within the Turonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Scalamagnus as a polycotylid member of the plesiosaur clade Leptocleidia.
rejected.quote: Clark, O'Keefe & Slack (2023) recovered Scalamagnus as a polycotylid member of the plesiosaur clade Leptocleidia
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'as a polycotylid member of the plesiosaur clade'
